```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`sikdr` implements the method of Xu, Jia, Chen and Chen, *Finite-Smoothing Efficiency and
Inference in Single-Index Models* (arXiv:2611.22384). The model is

$$Y = m(\beta^T X) + \varepsilon, \qquad \varepsilon \perp X .$$

Methods based on the conditional mean, such as MAVE, ignore the error distribution. When the
error is skewed or multimodal, its distribution also carries information about the
direction. SI-KDR refits the link at every candidate direction and scores the direction by
the leave-one-out kernel log-likelihood of the residuals.

## Fitting

```{r}
library(sikdr)
set.seed(1)
n <- 200
b0 <- c(1, 1, 0) / sqrt(2)
x <- matrix(rnorm(n * 3), n, 3)
e <- ifelse(runif(n) < 0.7, rnorm(n, -0.9, 0.5), rnorm(n, 2.1, 0.3))  # skewed, bimodal
y <- sin(2 * drop(x %*% b0)) + e
fit <- sikdr(x, y)
fit
```

The default `tuning = "trace"` ranks twenty smoothing tuples by the trace of the case-weight
covariance estimate at a preliminary fit. `tuning = "reference"` gives the reference rule
(SI-KDR-R). The angle between the estimate and the true direction, in degrees:

```{r}
acos(abs(sum(fit$beta * b0))) * 180 / pi
```

## Uncertainty

`vcov()` returns the case-weight covariance of the unit direction on the raw predictor
scale. It has rank $p - 1$ because the direction has unit length.

```{r}
round(vcov(fit), 5)
```

`sikdr_test()` gives the conditional score test of a candidate direction. Under Gaussian
predictors its $F$ distribution is exact for any single-index conditional response law,
including heteroscedastic ones.

```{r}
sikdr_test(fit, beta = rbind(truth = b0, wrong = c(1, 0, 0)))
```

`sikdr_confset()` inverts the test over random candidates near the estimate. The accepted
candidates form the confidence set.

```{r}
cs <- sikdr_confset(fit, draws = 50)
nrow(cs$accepted)
cs$max_angle * 180 / pi
```

## More predictors than observations

`sikdr_screen()` ranks predictors by distance correlation on one part of the sample and fits
SI-KDR on the other. When the screen keeps the support, the results above carry over to the
retained model.

```{r}
set.seed(2)
P <- 200
xh <- matrix(rnorm(n * P), n, P)
yh <- sin(2 * drop(xh[, 1:2] %*% c(1, 1)) / sqrt(2)) + e
sh <- sikdr_screen(xh, yh, size = 5, tuning = "reference", covariance = FALSE)
sh$selected
round(sh$beta[sh$selected], 3)
```

## Energy Efficiency benchmark

The package includes the UCI Energy Efficiency data. The code below predicts heating load
from seven inputs on random splits into 576 training and 192 test buildings and compares
SI-KDR, SI-KDR-R and mean MAVE (from the `MAVE` package). Each method reduces the inputs to
one index and predicts with the same kernel regression rule. It takes several minutes, so it
is not run here.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
data(energy)
X <- as.matrix(energy[, c("relative_compactness", "surface_area", "wall_area",
                          "overall_height", "orientation", "glazing_area",
                          "glazing_area_distribution")])
Y <- energy$heating_load
nmse <- function(fit_dir, xtr, ytr, xte, yte) {
  pred <- index_predict(xtr, ytr, xte, fit_dir)$pred
  mean((yte - pred)^2) / var(ytr)
}
set.seed(20261124)
splits <- lapply(1:30, function(i) sample.int(768, 576))  # all splits drawn before fitting
res <- t(sapply(splits, function(tr) {
  mu <- colMeans(X[tr, ])
  e <- eigen(crossprod(sweep(X[tr, ], 2, mu)) / 576, symmetric = TRUE)
  W <- e$vectors %*% (t(e$vectors) / sqrt(e$values))
  ztr <- sweep(X[tr, ], 2, mu) %*% W
  zte <- sweep(X[-tr, ], 2, mu) %*% W
  ys <- (Y[tr] - mean(Y[tr])) / sqrt(mean((Y[tr] - mean(Y[tr]))^2))
  mave <- drop(MAVE::mave.compute(ztr, ys, method = "MEANMAVE", max.dim = 1,
                                  screen = ncol(ztr))$dir[[1]])
  c(sikdr = nmse(sikdr(ztr, Y[tr], covariance = FALSE)$beta, ztr, Y[tr], zte, Y[-tr]),
    sikdr_r = nmse(sikdr(ztr, Y[tr], "reference", FALSE)$beta, ztr, Y[tr], zte, Y[-tr]),
    mave = nmse(mave, ztr, Y[tr], zte, Y[-tr]))
}))
colMeans(res)
```

Results of this code on our 30 splits (stored in the package):

```{r}
b <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "energy_benchmark.csv", package = "sikdr"))
round(colMeans(b[, c("sikdr", "sikdr_r", "mave")]), 5)
```

These splits are not the ones used in the paper, so the numbers differ from its table.

## Reference

Xu, J., Jia, Y., Chen, Y. and Chen, X. Finite-smoothing efficiency and inference in
single-index models. arXiv:2611.22384.
